disease_label_per_paper: Allopurinol-induced toxic epidermal necrolysis featuring almost 60% skin detachment
presentation_summary: 33-year-old man newly diagnosed with gout received allopurinol 250 mg daily for 10 days, then developed influenza-like prodrome with fever and throat pain.

The next day he developed worsening fever to 39.5 C and a pruritic generalized rash; exam later showed dusky erythematous, purpuric, irregular macules and atypical target lesions on trunk, face, and palms.
Skin progressed to flaccid bullae, positive Nikolsky sign, and sheet-like epidermal detachment over more than 60% BSA, exposing painful raw dermis.
Mucosal involvement included lips, oropharynx, genitalia, esophagus, gastrointestinal tract, and tracheobronchial surfaces with odynophagia, bleeding, and inability to eat or drink.

Admission vitals included temperature 38.9 C, BP 143/91 mmHg, and heart rate 121/min; labs showed WBC 13.7 x10^9/L, neutrophilia, AST 110 U/L, ALT 149 U/L, creatinine 94.3 umol/L, and CRP 27.80 mg/dL.

clinical_course.event: Prodrome with fever 38 C and throat pain while taking allopurinol; treated with amoxicillin and an oxicam NSAID.
Worsening fever 39.5 C and generalized pruritic rash; later evaluated with >60% BSA epidermal necrolysis and multisite mucosal sloughing.
After IVIG, corticosteroids, and supportive care, laboratory abnormalities normalized and skin re-epithelialization was achieved after 3 weeks.
